# ZettaPay — full reference

> Non-custodial crypto payment protocol. Funds go straight to the merchant's
> wallet — ZettaPay never holds keys or money. Self-hosted open-source listener
> or managed cloud, both non-custodial. Identity-free, zero telemetry, zero
> third party.

This is the expanded, RAG-friendly version of /llms.txt.
Everything below describes the real shipping product (@zettapay/listener v0.6.0).

## Core idea

ZettaPay is a payment listener you run yourself. You give it a public key
(a BIP-84 xpub for Bitcoin, an account xpub or a single receive address for
USDC/USDT on Base). It derives or reuses receive addresses, watches the chain,
and fires an HMAC-signed webhook to your backend the moment a payment confirms.
The funds settle directly to your wallet on-chain. ZettaPay never custodies
funds, never holds a signing key, and performs no identity checks.

Two ways to run it:

- Self-hosted: `npm i -g @zettapay/listener`, set a few env vars, run it on your
  own server. Open-source, MIT, auditable.
- Managed cloud: we run the same listener for you. Still non-custodial — funds
  go to your wallet, we only run the watcher.

## Supported assets

- Bitcoin (on-chain, BIP-84 native segwit). Amounts in satoshis.
- USDC on Base (chain id 8453). Amounts in USD.
- USDT on Base (chain id 8453). Amounts in USD.

There is no Solana and no Ethereum L1 support. Bitcoin and the two Base
stablecoins are the entire surface.

## Address modes

1. Per-invoice (xpub) mode — preferred. Each invoice derives a fresh address
   from the merchant's xpub (BIP-84 for BTC, m/44'/60' for Base). One address
   per invoice means payments are unambiguous.
2. Fixed-address mode — for wallets that cannot export an xpub. One shared
   receive address serves every invoice; the payer is identified by a unique
   per-invoice nonce encoded in the low decimals of the USD amount (e.g.
   29.000042). Fixed-address invoices expire after 1 hour so nonces recycle.

## HTTP API (the self-hosted listener)

Base URL: http://localhost:8787 by default (configurable). The listener is a
single dependency-light node:http server.

### POST /invoice

Creates a pending invoice. Auth: when `ZETTAPAY_API_KEY` is set, send it in the
`X-ZettaPay-Api-Key` header (compared in constant time). When unset, the
endpoint is open for local development and logs a warning at boot.

Bitcoin request:

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8787/invoice \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-ZettaPay-Api-Key: sk_live_...' \
  -d '{"amount_sats": 50000, "memo": "order 4711", "expires_in": 3600}'
```

Bitcoin 201 response (abridged):

```json
{
  "invoice_id": "inv_...",
  "chain": "btc",
  "asset": "BTC",
  "amount_btc": "0.0005",
  "receive_address": "bc1q...",
  "status": "pending",
  "derivation_path": "m/84'/0'/0'/0/12",
  "network": "mainnet",
  "amount_sats": 50000,
  "qr_uri": "bitcoin:bc1q...?amount=0.0005&label=order%204711",
  "verify_url": "https://mempool.space/address/bc1q...",
  "expires_at": "2026-06-01T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

USDC on Base request (xpub mode):

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8787/invoice \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-ZettaPay-Api-Key: sk_live_...' \
  -d '{"chain": "base", "amount_usd": 42.00}'
```

USDC/USDT on Base 201 response (abridged):

```json
{
  "invoice_id": "inv_...",
  "chain": "base",
  "asset": "USDC",
  "receive_address": "0x...",
  "status": "pending",
  "amount_usd": 42.0,
  "amount_usdc": "42",
  "amount_usdc_units": 42000000,
  "qr_uri": "ethereum:0x833589...@8453/transfer?address=0x...&uint256=42000000",
  "verify_url": "https://basescan.org/address/0x..."
}
```

USDT on Base request (fixed-address mode adds `"asset": "usdt"`):

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8787/invoice \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"chain": "base", "amount_usd": 42.00, "asset": "usdt"}'
```

In fixed-address mode the response also carries `"mode": "fixed-address"`, the
allocated `nonce`, the resolved `asset`, and the `token_address` the payer must
send. The exact `amount_usdc` includes the nonce in its low decimals.

Error responses use `{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "..." } }`:

- 400 invalid_amount / unsupported_chain / chain_disabled / base_disabled / asset_disabled / bad_body
- 401 unauthorized (bad or missing API key)
- 429 rate_limited (sliding-window per client IP; honors Retry-After)
- 503 capacity (fixed-address nonce pool temporarily exhausted)
- 500 create_failed

### GET /invoice/:id

Polls invoice status. Returns the same invoice shape as the create response
(without the one-shot fields like qr_uri). A pending invoice past its
`expires_at` is lazily flipped to `expired` on read.

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8787/invoice/inv_abc123
```

Status values: `pending`, `partial`, `confirmed`, `expired`, `failed`. On
payment the `tx_hash` and `paid_at` fields are populated.

### GET /health

Liveness and watcher state. No auth.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "ws_connected": true,
  "subscribed_count": 17,
  "last_event_at": "2026-06-01T11:59:00.000Z",
  "last_block_height": 845123,
  "uptime_s": 3600
}
```

## Webhooks

When a payment confirms, the listener POSTs a JSON event to your
`MERCHANT_WEBHOOK_URL` (HTTPS required; http://localhost allowed for dev with
@zettapay/receiver). The event body looks like:

```json
{
  "event": "invoice.confirmed",
  "invoice_id": "inv_...",
  "merchant_id": "mer_...",
  "chain": "btc",
  "asset": "BTC",
  "amount": "0.0005",
  "address": "bc1q...",
  "tx_hash": "...",
  "confirmations": 3,
  "confirmed_at": "2026-06-01T12:01:00.000Z"
}
```

Each delivery carries:

- `X-ZettaPay-Signature`: HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, hex-encoded,
  keyed by your `ZETTAPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
- `X-ZettaPay-Timestamp`: delivery time in unix milliseconds.
- `X-ZettaPay-Event-Id`: stable event id (use it for idempotency).
- `X-ZettaPay-Attempt`: 1-indexed attempt number.

Verify by recomputing `HMAC_SHA256(secret, rawBody)` and comparing in constant
time. The `@zettapay/sdk` `verifyWebhookSignature` and the `@zettapay/receiver`
CLI both do this for you. Confirmation tiers for BTC: 1/3/6 confirmations at
<$50 / <$500 / >=$500. Retries follow a Stripe-grade curve
(1s, 5s, 30s, 2m, 10m, 30m, 1h, 3h, 12h, 24h) up to 10 attempts.

## Configuration (env vars)

- ZETTAPAY_API_KEY — protects POST /invoice
- ZETTAPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET — HMAC signing key
- MERCHANT_WEBHOOK_URL — where confirmations are posted (HTTPS)
- MERCHANT_XPUB — BTC BIP-84 xpub (per-invoice mode)
- MERCHANT_XPUB_EVM — account xpub for USDC on Base (per-invoice mode)
- MERCHANT_EVM_ADDRESS + MERCHANT_EVM_CHAINS + MERCHANT_EVM_TOKENS — fixed-address mode

## Agent-native: @zettapay/mcp

`@zettapay/mcp` is an open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that runs
on the agent's or user's own machine and speaks to the LOCAL listener at
`http://localhost:8787`. It is fully self-hosted and non-custodial — it only
calls the user's own listener API; it never holds keys or funds.

MCP tools exposed:

- `create_invoice(amount_usd | amount_sats, chain, asset?)` → invoice id,
  receive address, exact amount, and QR/payment URI.
- `get_invoice_status(invoice_id)` → status and confirmations.
- `list_supported_assets()` → btc, usdc-base, usdt-base.

Claude Desktop config (claude_desktop_config.json):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "zettapay": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@zettapay/mcp"],
      "env": {
        "LISTENER_URL": "http://localhost:8787",
        "ZETTAPAY_API_KEY": "sk_live_..."
      }
    }
  }
}
```

With this, an AI agent can accept Bitcoin or USDC/USDT on Base in a single tool
call, against the user's own non-custodial listener.
